newsitem.title: UK: IRA suspect planned to black out Channel Tunnel.
newsitem.headline: IRA suspect planned to black out Channel Tunnel.

text.p: An IRA suspect shot dead by British police last week was planning to blow up the electricity supply to the Channel Tunnel between Britain and France, security sources said on Sunday.
The sources, quoted by the Sunday Times, said Diarmuid O'Neill was seen last July on the English coast reconnoitring an electricity sub-station which carries power to the tunnel.
It said O'Neill and another Irish Republican Army suspect were spotted by an undercover police surveillance team.

The IRA, fighting to oust Britain from Northern Ireland, had apparently decided against bombing the tunnel itself because security was too tight. But an attack on the electricity supply would have halted all traffic to the continent.
On Saturday, British police charged four suspects with conspiracy to cause explosions after raids in London that netted 10 tonnes of explosives.
Diarmuid O'Neill, who was described by his parents as "kind, unselfish and loving" was killed during the raids. His brother Shane was released from custody on Friday after five days questioning.

British authorities have been put on the defensive by reports that O'Neill was unarmed when he was shot, recalling the 1988 killing of three unarmed guerrillas by commandos in the British colony of Gibraltar.
Amnesty International has accused police of making misleading statements over the death of O'Neill and called for an independent judicial inquiry into the shooting.
